problem:
Find the coefficient of $(x-3)^{3}$ in the third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\frac{1}{x}$ about $x=3.$ Do not round the answer.

The coefficient of $(x-3)^{3}$ is
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The coefficient of $(x-3)^{3}$ is $\frac{1}{3!}{f}^{‴}(3).$ Let's compute the necessary derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{1}{x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =\frac{2}{{x}^{3}} \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =-\frac{6}{{x}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate ${f}^{‴}(3),$ which gives

$$
{f}^{‴}(3)=-\frac{6}{{3}^{4}}=-\frac{6}{81}=-\frac{2}{27}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{3!}{f}^{‴}(3)=\frac{1}{3!}\cdot (-\frac{2}{27})=-\frac{2}{6\cdot 27}=-\frac{1}{81}.
$$

So, the coefficient of $(x-3)^{3}$ is $-\frac{1}{81}.$
